messages.domainDnsUnverified: DNS for this hostname hasn't verified yet. Check the records, then re-run the check.
messages.routingUnsynced: The deploy succeeded but its edge route didn't sync, so the public URL may not resolve yet. Retrying re-runs just the routing step — it does not rebuild.
messages.certHttpsWillFail: HTTPS will fail for this hostname until a certificate is issued. Renewing re-runs issuance.
messages.partialServices: Some services failed to come up. The rest are live. Keep the release, or reject it to roll back to the previous one.
messages.partialNamedServices: These services failed: {services}. The rest are live. Keep the release, or reject it to roll back to the previous one.
messages.noCertOnServer: No usable HTTPS certificate was found on the server.
messages.dnsOtherServer: DNS points to a different server
messages.certEdgeFailed: Couldn't confirm a certificate ({detail}). Make sure the domain points at this server (a CDN like Cloudflare in front is fine) and ports 80/443 are reachable, then Verify again.
messages.certDnsUnresolved: {domain} doesn't resolve to this server yet — the DNS A record is missing or hasn't propagated. Wait for propagation, then retry from the Domains tab.
messages.certPort80Unreachable: Port 80 for {domain} isn't reachable from the internet — a firewall / cloud security group is blocking it, the domain doesn't point at this server, or another proxy is still bound to :80.
messages.certCloudflareProxy: Cloudflare's proxy is answering the certificate challenge for {domain} instead of forwarding it to this server: it redirects the request to HTTPS, then rejects the origin's TLS. Fix it one of three ways — set SSL/TLS → Overview to "Full" (not "Full (strict)") until the first certificate is issued, or turn the orange cloud off for this record until it is, or upload a Cloudflare Origin CA certificate from the Domains tab and skip Let's Encrypt entirely.
messages.certRedirect404: The challenge for {domain} was redirected from HTTP to HTTPS and then answered with a 404 — so whatever served it isn't routing that hostname. If {domain} is behind Cloudflare, its "Always Use HTTPS" is doing the redirect: set SSL/TLS → Overview to "Full" (not "Full (strict)") until the first certificate is issued, or turn the orange cloud off for this record. Otherwise check the A record points at this server and the domain is registered here. Nothing is occupying :80, so take-over / migrate will not help.
messages.certPort80NotAcme: Port 80 answered but not with our ACME challenge — another web server is still serving :80, so the takeover didn't complete. Re-run and choose take-over / migrate.
messages.certRateLimited: Let's Encrypt rate limit reached for {domain} — wait before retrying.
messages.certPortBindFailure: Couldn't start the certificate challenge listener for {domain} on port {port}: something on this server is already holding it. That port is used only while a certificate is being issued, so this is almost always a certificate run from an earlier attempt that hasn't exited — retry, and if it persists find the holder with  and stop it. Nothing was requested from Let's Encrypt, so this is not a DNS or routing problem.
messages.certFailedGeneric: certbot failed to issue a certificate for {domain}
messages.requestTimeout: Request timed out. The server took too long to respond.
messages.networkUnreachable: Cannot reach Openship. Check the connection and server availability.
